note: Parish-register holdings of HR-HDA-883, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga», at the Hrvatski državni arhiv in Zagreb. One row is a parish, a confession, a register type and the years that run: MKR rođeni (births/baptisms), MKV vjenčani (marriages), MKU umrli (deaths). Extracted as FACTS from the published inventory cited in `source` — the compilation is the author's and is not relicensed here.
undercount: THIS UNDERCOUNTS THE COLLECTION, AND A PARISH MISSING FROM IT IS NOT EVIDENCE THE ARCHIVE LACKS THAT PARISH. 2,503 rows were read from roughly 3,017 candidate lines; lines whose parish, type or date range could not be read unambiguously were dropped rather than guessed. Milić's own text puts the collection at 2,864 registers, 718 separated duplicates, 17 books of souls, 14 transcripts and 1 facsimile — so even a perfect parse would not be the whole of it. Read a gap here as our silence.
theRuleThatExplainsCroatianNils: WHY A CROATIAN REGISTER MAY BE IN NO ARCHIVE AT ALL. The Law on State Registers of 1 April 1946 provided that registers FROM 1860 ONWARD be handed to the civil registry offices (matični uredi), because they were needed in their work; the decision of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the People's Republic of Croatia of 13 May 1949 sent registers WITH ENTRIES UP TO 1860 to the competent archives for safekeeping. So for any Croatian parish, a person born after 1860 may have a baptism that never entered an archive: it is at the registry office, and the archive catalogue is silent for a reason that has nothing to do with the parish and nothing to do with whether the register survives. Both dates are Milić 2017, pp. 252.
